key_insight: Smaller frozen models can generate better rejection samples than a student’s own outputs, improving preference distillation while using less inference compute.
engineering_relevance: For large-scale training, reject data need not come from larger or self-generated models, enabling cheaper and more scalable preference optimization pipelines.
method: Derived a finite-horizon utility bound for DPO in a linearized feature model to characterize useful reject distributions.
Tested mixed reject sources from smaller and student-scale models, plus prompt shuffling and token shuffling ablations.
Compared lower-likelihood vs higher-likelihood candidate selection under the reference policy.
evidence_signal: Across student models from 7B to 72B, smaller frozen-model rejects trained stronger students than self-generated rejects on code generation and mathematical reasoning, before and after sequence-level KD.
watch_item: The benefit depends on preserving task structure and avoiding over-coupling to the reference policy, so naive noise or mismatched rejects may reduce utility.
paper_title: Smaller Models, Better Rejects: Preference Distillation Scaling
